children.name: Gigantopora lyncoides Ridley, 1881
children.description: Colonies encrusting, unilaminar (Fig. 4 A). Autozooids semierect and almost polygonal (0.698 – 0.974 – 1.097 mm long, n = 5, SD = 0.172; 0.455 – 0.535 – 0.623 mm wide, n = 5, SD = 0.066) (Fig. 4 B). Lepralioid frontal wall with nodular surface and small pseudopores (Fig. 4 B). Internal frontal wall without ring scar (Fig. 4 D). Spiramen large, placed at the suboral region of the peristome, occupying approximately half the width of the zooid (0.720 – 0.110 – 0.145 mm long, n = 5, SD = 0.032; 0.274 – 0.296 – 0.326 mm wide, n = 5, SD = 0.021); spiramen usually oval, slightly crescent or haltere-shaped, with thin edges projecting outward (Fig. 4 B). Primary orifice with arched distal margin, a pair of triangular condyles, and concave proximal margin. Peristome tubular, slightly inclined towards the distal region, tapering towards the edge, and completely covering the primary orifice (Fig. 4 B). Flattened secondary orifice with a trapezoidal proximal edge (0.157 – 0.186 – 0.222 mm long, n = 5, SD = 0.024; 0.231 – 0.237 – 0.249 mm wide, n = 5, SD = 0.007) (Fig. 4 B). Paired adventitious avicularia, latero-oral, positioned at the end of the peristome; rostrum acute, complete crossbar, curving at the distal edge of the peristome (0.164 – 0.194 – 0.218 mm long, n = 5, SD = 0.020; 0.078 – 0.084 – 0.090 mm wide, n = 5, SD = 0.004) (Fig. 4 B).
